clue.text: Clean up dog, perhaps, sweet little youngster

blocks.note: to mop is to clean up a floor or spill
a dog is one example of a household pet

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up after the dog and its adorable young owner.
explanation.definitionFit: A moppet is an affectionate word for a small, endearing child.

clue.text: Classic story of armoured unit suffering with flu

indicators.note: something suffering is damaged or knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; 'with' adds it to the other fodder

explanation.surface: A war tale in which a tank regiment is laid low by influenza.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two parts of the fodder; all fifteen letters are rearranged to give OUR MUTUAL FRIEND.
explanation.definitionFit: Our Mutual Friend is the last completed novel by Charles Dickens, a classic of English literature.

clue.text: Have groups of urban youths set on son?

blocks.note: a posse is slang for a gang of young people
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A worried parent asks whether gangs have been set upon their boy.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, one piece 'set on' another sits above it, so the gangs come first and the son below.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to own or hold it, a plain synonym for having it.

clue.text: Apparently nervous, time being such a ghoulish hour

blocks.note: T is the usual abbreviation for time
midnight is called the witching hour, when ghouls and witches are abroad

explanation.surface: Someone seems jumpy because it is nearly midnight, the spooky time.
explanation.definitionFit: Twitching means making small jerky movements, an outward sign that a person may be anxious or jittery.

clue.text: Skin treatment: couple it with dressing

indicators.note: dressing can mean arranging or setting in order, as troops dress their ranks, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: First-aid advice: put a medicated pad on the skin together with a bandage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' looks like a bandage in a first-aid scene, but it signals rearranging the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A poultice is a soft moist mass applied to the body to soothe inflammation or draw out infection.

clue.text: Almost perfect clothes for hobby

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: pure means flawless or perfect
a suit is a set of clothes

explanation.surface: Nearly ideal outfit to wear while pursuing a pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: A pursuit is an activity one follows for pleasure, such as a leisure pastime.

clue.text: Superior group displaced

blocks.note: up means higher, above others
a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: An elite clique has been ousted.
explanation.definitionFit: Upset can mean knocked over or moved out of place, as an upset vase is displaced.

clue.text: Pledge to welcome head of government that's put up in sailing ship

definitions.text: that's put up in sailing ship

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: to toast is to drink a pledge to someone's health
the Prime Minister heads the British government

explanation.surface: A vow to receive the national leader aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: the spar is raised up on a sailing vessel's mast. PM is the usual abbreviation for Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A topmast is the upper section of a mast, raised above the lower mast on a square-rigged vessel.

clue.text: Assurance over one round of cards is a swindle

blocks.note: confidence is self-assurance
in games like bridge, a trick is one round of cards played

explanation.surface: A card player's cockiness during a hand turns out to be a con.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidence trick is a fraud in which the victim's trust is won and then exploited.

clue.text: More flashy in short underwear

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: the full name of the bra

explanation.surface: Someone looks gaudier wearing skimpy lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short underwear' suggests BRA, but it is the full word that is shortened by one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassy describes something loud, showy and vulgar; brassier is its comparative form.

clue.text: Back on the floor?

blocks.note: surface reading: returning to the shop floor or dance floor
setter's reading: lying with one's back against the ground

explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like 'returning', but it is the body part touching the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine means lying face upward, so a person in that position rests on their back.

clue.text: Stubborn person has something afoot

blocks.note: first meaning: an obstinate individual, like the proverbially awkward animal
second meaning: a backless slipper or shoe worn on the foot

explanation.surface: An obstinate character is plotting something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afoot' usually means under way; here it means literally on a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a famously obstinate hybrid animal, hence a stubborn person, and a backless slip-on shoe.

clue.text: Reckon one comes in to support band leader

indicators.note: something coming in to another enters it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: to count is to reckon or calculate
a base is a support or foundation
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a newcomer will back the leader of a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band leader' reads as a musician directing a group, which is exactly what this jazz figure was.
explanation.definitionFit: Count Basie was an American jazz pianist who led one of the great swing big bands.

clue.text: Forced smile eating posh breakfast

indicators.note: something forced is strained and unnatural, so the letters are twisted out of order
eating means taking something inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
U stands for upper-class, as in U and non-U speech

explanation.surface: Someone grins politely while eating a fancy morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: SMILE is rearranged to MESLI and the U goes in after the M.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a cereal mix of oats, nuts and dried fruit, typically eaten in the morning.

clue.text: Formal agreements in dissertation to be read out

indicators.note: something read out is spoken, so we want a word that sounds like the clue's synonym

blocks.note: a treatise is a long formal written discussion

explanation.surface: Pacts contained in a thesis that is to be presented aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words differ only in their final syllable and are near-identical when spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Treaties are formally concluded and ratified agreements between states.

clue.text: Indicates they miss most of the stops

definitions.text: they miss most of the stops

blocks.note: first meaning: shows or conveys

blocks.clueFragment: they miss most of the stops
blocks.note: second meaning: fast trains that call at only a few stations

explanation.surface: A sign suggests some people overlook nearly all the punctuation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops' sounds like full stops, but they are railway stations.
explanation.definitionFit: To express a feeling is to show it, and express trains skip most intermediate stations.

clue.text: No one left, since you insist

blocks.note: first meaning, read cryptically: everybody is on the right, nobody on the left
second meaning: a reluctant 'okay, then'

explanation.surface: Fine, everyone has gone, if you must know.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' seems to mean departed; it is the opposite of right.
explanation.definitionFit: Said grudgingly, the phrase means 'okay, I agree', a concession made because someone keeps pressing.

clue.text: Basic facts that could end up cooked?

definitions.text: Basic facts that could end up cooked?

blocks.clueFragment: Basic facts that could end up cooked?
blocks.note: surface reading: simple ingredients that might be heated for a meal

blocks.clueFragment: Basic facts that could end up cooked?
blocks.note: setter's reading: unprocessed figures that a dishonest analyst might falsify

explanation.walkthrough: To cook the books is to falsify figures, so 'cooked' means doctored, and uncooked food is the opposite state.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw data are unprocessed measurements or figures, the basic material before analysis or manipulation.

clue.text: Youth once fails to get soft toys

blocks.note: a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress
an engine that fails dies

explanation.surface: A young person in the past cannot obtain cuddly playthings.
explanation.definitionFit: Teddies are stuffed toy bears, the classic plush toy given to children.

clue.text: Abrasive, turn up with computer equipment

indicators.note: to turn the next word means to read it the other way round

blocks.note: taken as written
mice are pointing devices used with computers

explanation.surface: An abrasive person arrives bringing their PC gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' looks like a phrasal verb meaning arrive, but 'turn' acts only on the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumice is a light porous volcanic rock used to scrub and smooth skin, an abrasive.

clue.text: This comes under the hammer, two graduates holding the edge

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so one piece sits within the others

blocks.note: an MA and a BA, a master's and a bachelor's degree
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: An auction lot: an item sold by two academics on the brink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under the hammer' suggests an auction, but a marimba's bars are struck with mallets.
explanation.definitionFit: A marimba is a large xylophone-like instrument whose wooden bars are played with beaters.

clue.text: This admission to castle is a let-down

definitions.text: This admission to castle is a let-down

blocks.clueFragment: This admission to castle is a let-down
blocks.note: surface reading: the entry fee to a fortress proved disappointing

blocks.clueFragment: This admission to castle is a let-down
blocks.note: setter's reading: the way into a fortress is lowered to let people in

explanation.walkthrough: 'admission' means entrance, not a ticket, and 'let-down' is literal: it is lowered over the moat.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawbridge is a hinged bridge over a moat, lowered to give entry to a castle.

clue.text: Keepsake from barrel I collected

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the following words as they stand

blocks.note: the run of letters sits across the three words

explanation.surface: A souvenir taken from a cask that someone gathered.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object kept as a reminder of the past, a memento or souvenir.

clue.text: 18 letters returned in the course of duty

indicators.note: returned means sent back the way it came, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the alphabet from A to R spans exactly eighteen letters

explanation.surface: Eighteen pieces of post sent back while someone was working.
explanation.walkthrough: '18' is not a cross-reference to 18 down; A TO R covers the first eighteen letters of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a list setting out the order in which people take turns at their tasks.

clue.text: Remember to phone again

blocks.note: first meaning: bring back to mind
second meaning: call someone back

explanation.surface: A reminder note: don't forget to ring back.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall is to bring a memory back, and also to telephone someone a second time.

clue.text: Sleep on this problem? No way

definitions.text: Sleep on this problem? No way

blocks.clueFragment: Sleep on this problem? No way
blocks.note: surface reading: refusing advice to sleep on a difficulty before deciding

blocks.clueFragment: Sleep on this problem? No way
blocks.note: setter's reading: a condition in which sleep is impossible

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleep on it' is advice to delay a decision; here the problem itself is a lack of sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia is the chronic inability to fall or stay asleep, a disorder of sleep.

clue.text: Lender makes these improvements

blocks.note: first meaning: loans of money paid out early
second meaning: steps forward or progress

explanation.surface: A bank's moneylender carries out upgrades.
explanation.definitionFit: Advances are sums lent before they are due, and also forward steps or developments.

clue.text: Vivacious agent going round lifeboat

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a spy is a secret agent
Noah's ark saved life from the Flood

explanation.surface: A lively secret agent circles a rescue boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Noah's ark is the vessel that saved life from the Flood, hence a lifeboat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparky describes someone lively and spirited, full of energy and wit.
